Engineering Methodology


## 
The 5-Stage Statutory & Engineering Lifecycle



Consolidated lifecycle ensuring legal immunity, physical readiness, and timely bi-annual Form B endorsement.










01 
Hazard Audit 

Physical on-site review of installed water storage, booster pumps, riser integrity, alarms, and escape corridors.




Scope Documented 





02 
Engineering Scope 

Bill of Quantities (BOQ), code-compliant equipment specifications, and transparent line-item proposal submitted to committee.




Quotation Issued 





03 
Turnkey Execution 

Piping fabrication, valve replacement, booster pump servicing, detector loop rewiring, and extinguisher refilling by 25+ crew.




Fitter Crew Deployed 





04 
Pressure Testing 

Hydrostatic pressure testing of riser columns, landing valve flow measurement, and panel alarm simulation under load.




Tested Under Load 





05 
Form B Filings 

Statutory Form B certificate issuance in January and July cycles, signed and sealed by Class D licensed agency.




Bi-Annual Renewal

ENGINEERING EXCELLENCE • CLASS D GOVT. AGENCY 



# 
Fire Safety Should Be Ready When It Matters


Samarth Fire Protection System helps buildings and businesses install, maintain and use fire safety equipment. Our work includes fire alarm systems, fire fighting systems, equipment supply, site checks and practical safety training.



















DOCUMENTARY RECORD • MUMBAI 
Explaining cylinder pressure gauges and the PASS operational protocol to society staff. 










OUR STORY & PHILOSOPHY


## 
Why We Refuse To Be Just Another Equipment Vendor



In Mumbai's high-density urban landscape, thousands of residential housing societies and commercial towers install fire fighting systems simply to fulfill initial building clearance paperwork. Years later, valves seize, booster pump panels corrode, alarm zones are muted due to false triggers, and extinguishers expire unnoticed.



Samarth Fire Protection System was founded to solve this systemic gap. We operate not as a retail storefront selling painted red canisters, but as an audit-led engineering agency. We inspect physical pipe loops, trace shorted detector loops, pressure-test risers up to operating thresholds, and train resident communities so that equipment works reliably in an emergency.



Our Core Tenet: 
"We evaluate what your property actually requires under the Maharashtra Fire Prevention Act and NBC standards. We never propose redundant equipment or unverified work."

THE PHILOSOPHY BEHIND THE ASSESSMENT 

## 
"Fire Safety Cannot Be Solved Remotely from a Product Catalog."




In Mumbai's dense urban topology of high-rise residential societies and complex commercial parks, fire safety is frequently misunderstood as a mere procurement exercise. Society committees often purchase extinguishers or sign basic maintenance contracts without knowing if their water risers hold pressure or if their pumps will start when power trips.




As a Maharashtra Fire Services Licensed Agency Director with over 8 years of engineering practice , Sameer M. Kangutkar founded Samarth Fire Protection System to establish an engineering-led inspection protocol. His approach analyzes the entire life-safety ecosystem: structural egress routes, pressurized riser manifolds, smoke barrier integrity, detector sensitivity, and human emergency readiness.




The Assessment-First Doctrine: "Before proposing a single valve or cylinder, our engineers physically walk the premises. We inspect the booster pump cut-off pressure, test the furthest roof hydrant landing valve, examine refuge area ventilation, and interview the on-site security guards. Only then do we prepare an accurate, transparent engineering plan."



Under Sameer's leadership, Samarth Fire has successfully delivered installations and compliance audits for critical national infrastructure such as a Central Government Nuclear Facility Complex , premier commercial hubs like a Leading Diamond Bourse Commercial Exchange in BKC , educational institutions like a Prominent International IB School Campus in Mulund , and more than 500 cooperative housing societies across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region.





### Direct Consultant Walkthrough


If your building committee is facing an upcoming Form B renewal deadline or has experienced recurring faults in your fire alarm system, you can request an advisory walkthrough directly with Sameer.




Schedule Founder Site Walkthrough

Title: Maharashtra Fire Service Class D License | Samarth Fire Protection

Agency Credentials 



# 
Government Licensing & Compliance 



Directorate of Maharashtra Fire & Emergency Services • Official Class D Licenced Agency
















## Why Government Licensing Matters



Under the Maharashtra Fire Prevention and Life Safety Measures Act, 2006 , fire fighting installations, alarm loops, and suppression systems can only be executed, repaired, or certified by agencies licensed by the state government.




Any fire safety work done by unlicensed contractors, retailers, or electrical installers is considered non-compliant. Such works are legally invalid and cannot be used to obtain provisional or final fire clearances or to file Form B clearances.




AUTHORIZED COMPLIANCE CAPABILITIES


• 
Form A Authorization: Issued on completion of new system installations. It verifies that the equipment matches municipal rules and allows the society to obtain a Fire NOC. 



• 
Form B Authorization: Issued twice a year (every January and July) following a physical safety check. This certifies that existing systems remain fully operational. 






Samarth Fire Protection System maintains license MFS/LA/RF-34/RD-35 (Class D) in active, verified status. This ensures that every audit we conduct and every certificate we sign carries official authority.

System Schematic Line-Work

##
Dual-Zone Wet Riser & Booster Configuration

High-rise structures demand dedicated hydraulic vertical mains permanently charged with pressurized water. Our engineering team calculates static pressure heads, frictional line loss, and flow delivery to ensure compliant coverage at every landing valve.

- 01. Underground reservoir suction manifold with anti-vortex plates

- 02. Staged electric, diesel, and jockey pump automation loop

- 03. Non-return check valves and calibrated pressure relief stations

- 04. Dual 63mm gunmetal landing valves per floor landing

[Schematic Specification] Illustrative engineering schematic — actual riser pipe diameters, pump ratings, and riser zoning vary by site structure and hydraulic plan.

Engineering Scope Matrix

##
Active Fire Suppression Capabilities

All installations, retrofits, and overhauls executed strictly under Directorate of Maharashtra Fire Services statutory licensing.

DISCIPLINE 01
NBC 2016 Compliant

###
Wet & Dry Riser Networks

Vertical galvanized heavy-grade steel piping networks connecting basement or podium pump manifolds to terrace storage tanks. Equipped with calibrated landing valves on each floor landing and external ground breeching inlets for municipal fire brigade connections.

Components: Galvanized pipes, 63mm gunmetal valves, air release valves

Verification: Hydrostatic pressure testing to applicable standards

DISCIPLINE 02
Automated Suppression

###
Automatic Sprinkler Arrays

Thermally triggered quartzoid glass-bulb sprinkler networks covering basement car parking, podium levels, and commercial work floors. Integrated with zone control valves, waterflow indicator switches, and localized alarm gongs for rapid containment.

Configuration: Pendant, upright, and sidewall head distribution

Monitoring: Electrical flow switches linked to main fire alarm panel

DISCIPLINE 03
Mechanical Automation

###
Booster Pump Staging & Controls

Triple-tier pump station synchronization comprising main electric motor pump, auto-start auxiliary diesel engine fallback, and continuous jockey pump for line pressure maintenance. Staged automatically through sensory pressure switch manifolds.

Control Panel: Microprocessor-based auto-sequencing control cabinet

Testing: Weekly auto-start cycle calibration and battery health checks

DISCIPLINE 04
First-Aid Response

###
Yard Hydrants & Hose Reels

External compound yard hydrant ring mains with standposts and instantaneous couplings for perimeter defense. Internal swing-drum first-aid hose reels equipped with non-kinking hydraulic hose and dual shut-off jet/spray branch nozzles.

Hose Drum: 19mm/25mm swing-arm drums with 30-meter hose length

Cabinetry: Weatherproof MS/CRCA enamel-coated landing cabinets

Statutory Reference

##
Frequently Asked Technical Questions

### What is the functional difference between a Wet Riser and a Dry Riser?

A Wet Riser is permanently charged with water under constant pressure from an underground/overhead reservoir and automated booster pumps, ready for instantaneous water delivery during an emergency.

A Dry Riser remains empty under normal building conditions and is only pressurized when the municipal fire brigade arrives and pumps water into the external four-way breeching inlet at the building entrance.

### What hydraulic pressure must a residential fire hydrant system maintain?

Under the National Building Code (NBC) 2016 Part 4 and Maharashtra Fire Prevention standards, high-rise wet riser networks must maintain the prescribed statutory running pressure at the topmost landing valve outlet while sustaining the designated hydrostatic test pressure across the riser column and pump manifold without leakage or pressure loss.

### How frequently must fire fighting pumps and risers be inspected for Form B compliance?

Pumps should undergo routine weekly test runs to ensure starter panels, batteries, and diesel engines engage without delay. Complete physical servicing, gland repacking, valve lubrication, and statutory Form B certification must be completed and submitted twice yearly (in January and July) under Maharashtra Fire Prevention and Life Safety Measures Act rules.

Maharashtra Fire Services • Class D Authorized





# 
Fire Detection & Alarm Systems 




Authorized Class D installers of addressable smoke detection loops, optical sensors, manual call stations, fault loop rectification, and central repeater panels across Mumbai.






Get a Quote for this System 



Troubleshoot Panel Faults 








Licence: MFS/LA/RF-34/RD-35 




IS 2189 & NBC 2016 Compliant 

















Alarm Telemetry


Optical smoke sensor continuity testing and addressable loop troubleshooting on floor landing.






























Engineering Definition: Fire detection and alarm systems are automated electrical sensor networks that continuously monitor for airborne combustion particles, thermal spikes, or manual emergency button inputs. Samarth Fire designs, tests, and repairs both addressable and conventional networks under a Class D government license.













TECHNICAL CAPABILITIES 

## Detection Loop Specifications


We isolate open ground faults, replace dead optical heads, and synchronize sounder hooters with staircase pressurization dampers.









01



### Addressable Control Panels


Multi-loop microprocessor panels capable of pinpointing the exact room, floor, or electrical riser where smoke particulate density exceeds safety thresholds.







02



### Optical & Thermal Sensors


Photoelectric smoke detectors for living areas and corridors, rate-of-rise heat sensors for kitchen and generator rooms, and duct sensors for HVAC lines.







03



### Manual Call Points (MCP)


Break-glass and push-type manual triggers located adjacent to every staircase exit landing, equipped with dual-action reset keys and visual status LEDs.







04



### Sounders, Strobes & Voice


Electronic hooters with integrated xenon or LED visual strobe lights (90+ dB sound output) and automated multi-lingual voice evacuation audio controllers.













LOOP TROUBLESHOOTING 

### Eliminating False Alarms





Repeated phantom alarm buzzing leads building occupants to disable the main control panel. Our engineers perform circuit megger tests and ultrasonic detector head cleaning to permanently resolve ghost alarms.

COMMON QUESTIONS 

## Frequently Asked Questions







### Why does our fire alarm panel beep continuously with a trouble light?


A trouble light usually signals an open loop circuit, an end-of-line resistor failure, a disconnected smoke detector head, or a drained 24V backup battery pack. Our engineers trace the zone wiring with digital multimeters and restore healthy supervision without costly panel replacements.







### Can addressable smoke detectors be added to an existing conventional system?


Conventional panels cannot address individual detectors by digital ID. However, we can integrate addressable zone interface modules or transition your property smoothly to a hybrid addressable master panel while utilizing existing fire-resistant wiring conduits.







### How often should optical smoke detectors be cleaned?


In urban environments like Mumbai, construction dust and humidity accumulate in optical sensor chambers over time. IS 2189 mandates semi-annual detector head vacuuming and calibration to maintain optical sensitivity without triggering false alarm hooters.

Engineering Definition: Portable fire extinguishers are first-line defensive appliances designed to suppress incipient fires before sprinkler systems activate. Samarth Fire supplies, refills, and hydraulically tests all chemical types under IS 2190 guidelines with tamper-evident seals and inspection verification tags.













TECHNICAL CAPABILITIES 

## Cylinder Engineering Specifications


Every refilled extinguisher undergoes nitrogen pressurization, scale weighing, and leak immersion testing before site delivery.









01



### ABC Dry Chemical Powder


Monoammonium Phosphate (MAP 50% / 90%) pressurized with dry nitrogen gas. Multi-purpose suppression for Class A (wood), Class B (fuels), and Class C (electrical).







02



### Carbon Dioxide (CO₂) Gas


Seamless manganese steel or carbon-steel cylinders filled with liquid CO₂ gas for server rooms, elevator shafts, electrical panels, and clean laboratories.







03



### Mechanical Foam (AFFF)


Aqueous Film Forming Foam creates an airtight blanket over diesel generator rooms, solvent tanks, and parking oil leaks, cutting oxygen supply instantly.







04



### Hydraulic Pressure Test (HPT)


Mandatory shell expansion testing at 30 to 250 kg/cm² to detect micro-cracks and seam fatigue before recharging cylinders with working pressures.

COMMON QUESTIONS

### How can we verify if our building fire extinguishers need refilling?


Check the dial pressure gauge on the cylinder valve: if the needle rests in the red discharge zone or if the statutory inspection tag is older than 12 months, immediate refilling and re-pressurization are required under IS 2190 regulations.







### Do you provide standby cylinders during refilling pickup?


Yes. To ensure your housing society or commercial facility is never left vulnerable or unprotected while cylinders undergo hydraulic testing at our workshop, we provide standby replacement extinguishers.







### What is the difference between ABC Powder and CO₂ extinguishers?


ABC powder smothers solid combustibles, liquid fires, and electrical components with a fine non-conductive chemical layer. CO₂ gas displaces oxygen and cools electrical components without leaving chemical residues, making it ideal for servers and high-value equipment.

Engineering Definition: Passive fire protection contains active fires and lethal smoke within their compartment of origin for a specified duration (typically 60 to 120 minutes), preserving escape stairwells and structural integrity. Samarth Fire supplies and installs certified barriers under Class D regulatory oversight.

We stop vertical smoke spread through open service shafts and install certified fire doors on escape stairwells.

COMMON QUESTIONS 

## Frequently Asked Questions







### Why are fire doors required on residential staircase landings?


Stairways are the primary emergency escape route for occupants during a building fire. Under NBC 2016, 120-minute rated fire doors with self-closers ensure that smoke and toxic heat from a burning corridor cannot enter the staircase enclosure while residents evacuate.







### Can fire doors be wedged open for fresh air ventilation?


No. Propping fire doors open is a severe municipal code violation. A wedged-open door permits lethal smoke to suffocate the entire staircase within 90 seconds. If natural ventilation is required, electromagnetic hold-open devices linked to the fire alarm system must be installed.







### What happens if service duct penetrations are left unsealed?


Electrical cable shafts and plumbing ducts that pass through concrete floor slabs act as natural chimneys. Fire in a lower floor basement will draft straight up through unsealed floor gaps, igniting upper levels within minutes. Intumescent firestop pillows expand under heat to create a rock-hard seal.

Statutory Law Requirement: Under Section 3(1) of the Maharashtra Fire Prevention and Life Safety Measures Act, 2006, the owner or occupier of every building must maintain fire prevention systems in good repair and submit a statutory certificate (Form B) issued by a Licensed Agency twice a year in January and July to the Chief Fire Officer.













AUDIT METHODOLOGY 

## Form B Certification Scope


Our audit is an engineering verification of operational pressure, pump synchronization, and escape path clearances.









01



### Walkthrough Safety Audit


Physical verification of terrace water tanks, landing valves, hose reels, fire doors, refuge floor emergency lights, and unobstructed staircase passageways.







02



### Pressure & Pump Test


Testing electric booster, diesel backup, and jockey pump starters; logging hydrostatic running pressure at the highest landing valve to confirm 3.5 bar minimum.







03



### Defect Rectification Plan


Itemized diagnostic report identifying jammed landing valves, discharged extinguishers, or alarm open loops with rapid turn-around servicing quotes.







04



### Form B Statutory Signing


Execution of official Form B certificate under Maharashtra Fire Services licence number MFS/LA/RF-34/RD-35 for municipal submission and legal compliance.

### What is the difference between Form A and Form B?


Form A is the initial certificate issued when a new fire prevention system is installed or commissioned, certifying that work conforms to approved plans. Form B is the recurring bi-annual certificate confirming that existing systems remain fully operational, pressurized, and maintained twice each year.







### Who is authorized to issue a Form B certificate in Maharashtra?


Only a Licensed Agency holding a valid license issued by the Directorate of Maharashtra Fire Services (such as Samarth Fire Protection System, Licence No. MFS/LA/RF-34/RD-35) is legally authorized to inspect, sign, and issue Form B certificates under the Maharashtra Fire Act.







### What happens if a building fails its initial Form B inspection?


When an inspection identifies defects, we document the findings and recommend corrective work. The relevant certificate can be issued only after the required checks, repairs and retesting support the applicable compliance requirements; a repair booking or quotation is not a certificate.

Title: Fire Safety FAQs for Buildings, Societies & Businesses | Samarth Fire
Last updated: 2026-11-04

Forms & compliance 
Extinguishers 
Fire systems & AMC 
People & training 





## Forms and Maharashtra compliance



### What is the difference between Form A and Form B?
Form A is the licensed agency’s certificate regarding compliance of the fire-prevention and life-safety measures required in a building or part of it; it is commonly relevant to the installation or approval stage. Form B is the periodic certificate about maintenance of those measures during the preceding six months. They have different purposes. The building’s approved fire plan and current Maharashtra rules determine which systems and records apply.
See the Maharashtra Fire & Emergency Services Acts and Rules and the Directorate circulars .



### Is Form B the same as a Fire NOC?
No. Form B is a periodic maintenance certificate under the Maharashtra fire-safety framework. A Fire NOC or fire approval is a separate approval or clearance for the relevant stage and purpose. Do not treat a Form B certificate as a replacement for a building’s required fire approval.



### When is Form B due in Maharashtra?
The Directorate’s 7 July 2026 Guidelines to issue Form B describe the six-month reporting periods: the January Form B covers 1 July to 31 December of the preceding year; the July Form B covers 1 January to 30 June of the current year. Form B validity then runs until the next scheduled maintenance under the applicable Indian Standard and/or until the next Form B is issued, subject to the maintenance contract. The six-month filing period does not replace equipment-level maintenance intervals. Confirm the local submission route with the Chief Fire Officer or nominated officer.
Read the Directorate’s 7 July 2026 Form B guidelines (PDF) , the official circular list and the Act and Rules .



### What documents may be needed for a Form B submission?
The Directorate’s July 2026 guidance lists a minimum supporting set: a covering letter on the owner/occupier’s letterhead; the applicable Form B appendices for the installed systems; an AMC/CAMC order copy (without the price) or work-order confirmation stating the period, systems and agency; signed service and test reports for the relevant period; the latest site inspection report digitally signed by both parties; and a copy of the licensed agency’s valid licence. The digital signature on Form B must match the signature on the licence. The prescribed Form B wording must not be changed. The circular also says the listed documents are a minimum, not an exhaustive set.
Check the latest Maharashtra Fire Services circulars before filing.



### What is Form B-1? Is it the same as Form B?
No. The Maharashtra Fire Prevention and Life Safety Measures (Amendment) Rules, 2025 introduced Form A-1 for the certificate confirming installation of an Automated Continuous Monitoring System (ACMS), and Form B-1 for the related twice-yearly maintenance certificate for fire-fighting systems monitored through ACMS. Form A/B and Form A-1/B-1 serve different purposes; the ACMS forms apply where the relevant ACMS provisions apply to the building.
Read the 2025 Amendment Rules (PDF) and the official Acts and Rules page .



### Who can issue the maintenance certificate?
Form B sits within the licensed-agency framework under Maharashtra fire-safety law. Check that the agency has a current Directorate licence covering the relevant systems, and make sure the prescribed form, annexures and digital-signature requirements are followed. A quotation, work order or ordinary service note is not a Form B certificate.









## Fire extinguishers and equipment checks



### How often should a portable fire extinguisher be checked?
IS 2190:2024 says extinguishers should be checked when first placed in service and thereafter at approximately 90-day intervals, with more frequent checks where circumstances require. Checks include location, access, visibility, legible instructions, seals, fullness, damage or leakage, the pressure indicator where provided, and the inspection and HPT tags. Follow the current standard and the equipment manufacturer’s instructions.
Reference: BIS IS 2190:2024 .



### How often does a fire extinguisher need maintenance?
IS 2190:2024 states that, except for the cases identified in its Annex D, extinguishers are to receive maintenance once a year and not less than six months apart, as well as at hydrostatic testing or when an inspection shows it is needed. The specific procedure depends on the extinguisher type. A visual check is not a substitute for maintenance by a competent service provider.
Reference: BIS standard details for IS 2190:2024 .



### What is HPT for a fire extinguisher?
HPT means hydrostatic pressure testing. It checks whether the extinguisher cylinder can safely withstand the required test pressure. The interval and procedure depend on the extinguisher category and the applicable standard. Do not apply one generic “every three” or “every five years” interval to every cylinder; check its type, markings, service history and the current IS 2190 requirements.



### Can I use a water extinguisher on an electrical or oil fire?
Do not apply a water jet to energised electrical equipment or burning oil. It can cause electric shock or spread burning liquid. Raise the alarm, isolate power or fuel only if it is safe to do so, and use only an extinguisher suitable for the fuel and listed on its label. If the fire is growing or the escape route is not clear, evacuate and call emergency services.









## Fire alarm, hydrant systems, audits and AMC



### What should a building fire safety audit cover?
A building-specific review can cover the installed fire pumps, hydrants and wet risers, hose reels, sprinklers, extinguishers, alarm and detection systems, fire doors, exits, emergency lighting, signage, access routes, housekeeping and maintenance records. The scope depends on the building’s use, height, approved fire plans and applicable requirements. A generic checklist cannot confirm that a building is compliant.



### Is there one pressure value for every fire hydrant system?
No. Required pressure and flow depend on the building, system design, hydraulic calculations, pump duty, outlet location, approved documents and applicable standards. Use the design and test criteria for that specific installation. Do not set or advertise a universal pressure value for every building.



### What should a fire system AMC include?
An AMC should clearly state which systems and locations are covered, the inspection and test schedule, the work included, parts or consumables excluded, how faults are reported, response arrangements, service-report format and how defects are closed. Fire alarm, hydrant, pump, sprinkler and passive fire systems have different checks, so the contract should name the actual equipment rather than just say “complete fire AMC.”



### What should we do when a fire alarm panel shows a fault?
Do not switch off, bypass or repeatedly reset a panel simply to silence the buzzer. Follow your building’s response plan, check for signs of an actual fire from a safe location, record the message or affected zone/device, inform the responsible person and arrange a competent technician. If there is smoke, heat or a suspected fire, activate the emergency response and evacuate as required.



### What is the difference between a wet riser and a dry riser?
A wet riser is normally kept charged with water and connected to the building’s fire-water supply and pumps. A dry riser is normally empty and is filled by the fire brigade through its inlet when required. Which arrangement is required depends on the building design and applicable fire requirements.









## Fire drills, first aid and service coverage



### What should a housing society fire drill include?
A practical drill should follow the building’s approved emergency plan. It normally includes a coordinator and floor wardens, resident communication, safe exit routes, an assembly point, arrangements for people needing assistance, headcount and a written review of what should improve. Equipment demonstrations should be planned and supervised by competent trainers. The Directorate’s July 2026 Form B guidance also refers to periodic mock drills and supporting records.



### Does Samarth Fire provide first aid and CPR training?
Yes. The company catalogue lists first aid and CPR training, fire safety demonstrations and mock drills among its services. The session content and audience can be discussed when requesting a programme for a workplace, school or housing society.



### Does Samarth Fire supply and maintain extinguishers outside Mumbai?
Yes. Samarth Fire welcomes Pan-India enquiries for fire extinguisher supply, installation and maintenance, including towns and rural locations. Site visits, travel, delivery and service arrangements are confirmed for each location before the work is accepted.



### How do I request a quote or site visit?
Use the quotation form or site-visit request form . Share your location, property type, systems involved and the service you need. The Samarth Fire team will contact you to discuss the requirements and coordinate timing.









## Official references used for these answers

Maharashtra fire-safety requirements can change and may differ by building type and approved plan. Check the latest Directorate publications and the current BIS standard before relying on a checklist.

Title: Fire Safety Glossary: Terms Every Building Owner Should Know | Samarth Fire
Last updated: 2026-11-02

Terms are grouped by topic. Each links to a fuller guide where one exists.



## Compliance & regulation


Form A A certificate issued by a licensed fire agency confirming fire-protection systems have been installed and completed as per the approved plan. Read more in our Form B guide .

Form B A statutory six-monthly certificate (filed in January and July) confirming that installed fire-safety systems remain operational and maintained, required under the Maharashtra Fire Prevention and Life Safety Measures Act, 2006.

NOC (No Objection Certificate) A clearance issued by the fire department confirming no objection to a building's occupation, based on its fire-safety provisions at the time of inspection.

Class D Licensed Agency A category of fire-safety agency licensed by the Directorate of Maharashtra Fire & Emergency Services to install, inspect and certify specific classes of fire-protection systems. Samarth Fire holds licence MFS/LA/RF-34/RD-35 .

Competent authority The government body — typically the Directorate of Maharashtra Fire & Emergency Services or local Chief Fire Officer — with legal authority over fire-safety approvals for a given area.




## Fire-fighting systems


Wet riser A vertical pipe kept permanently filled with pressurised water so a hose can be connected on any floor without delay. See the full wet riser guide .

Dry riser A vertical pipe left empty until the fire brigade pumps water into it through a ground-level inlet, typically used where a permanent water supply is impractical.

Landing valve The valve and outlet on each floor where a hose connects to the riser pipe.

Jockey pump A small pump that maintains constant line pressure so the larger main and standby pumps don't start and stop for minor pressure drops.

Booster pump A pump that increases water pressure to meet the flow and pressure required at the highest or most distant outlet in a system.

Yard hydrant / landing valve An outdoor hydrant point, typically along a building's perimeter, giving the fire brigade external access to the water supply.




## Detection & alarm


Conventional fire alarm panel A panel that reports an alarm by zone (area), not by individual device. See conventional vs addressable .

Addressable fire alarm panel A panel that identifies the exact device in alarm, down to its location, rather than just the zone.

Manual call point (MCP) A break-glass or push-button unit that lets a person manually trigger the fire alarm.

Heat detector A detector that triggers on a rapid rise in temperature or a fixed threshold, often used where smoke detectors would give frequent false alarms (kitchens, boiler rooms).




## Extinguishers


HPT (Hydrostatic Pressure Testing) A periodic pressure test of an extinguisher cylinder to confirm it can safely hold its rated pressure, required every 3–5 years depending on type under IS 2190.

ABC dry powder A general-purpose extinguishing agent effective on Class A, B and C fires. See the extinguisher types guide .

P.A.S.S. technique The standard method for operating a portable extinguisher: Pull the pin, Aim at the base of the fire, Squeeze the handle, Sweep side to side.




## Passive protection


Fire-rated door (FRD) A door assembly tested and certified to resist fire for a specific duration (e.g. 2-hour rated), typically fitted with an automatic door closer to stay shut.

Fire damper A device inside ductwork that closes automatically in a fire to stop flame and smoke spreading through the ventilation system.

Penetration seal / fire stop Fire-resistant sealant or collar used where pipes or cables pass through a fire-rated wall or floor, restoring the barrier's rating at that opening.

CASE LOG 01 • ALARM RECTIFICATION




## 
F Residency Cooperative Housing Society


Location: Malad East, Mumbai • Building: 18-Storey Residential CHS 










Client Name 
F Residency CHS 



Property Type 
Residential Tower 



Initial Status 
False Buzzer Alarms 



Handover Status 
Form B Certified 







### 1. Initial Requirement


The society's master alarm control panel was continuously triggering false emergency buzzer warnings. Several optical detector loops had ground-faulted behind corridor false ceilings, and the Public Address (PA) amplifier suffered from persistent electrical 50Hz hums during announcements.







### 2. Scope of Work & Execution


Instead of requiring the society to scrap and replace the entire panel system, our electronic technicians conducted megger loop isolation across all 18 floors. We isolated 2 shorted detector bases caused by monsoon moisture condensation, replaced corroded terminal plates, balanced ground impedance, and rewired the pre-amplifier input.







### 3. Verified Outcome & Handover


All 4 master loop zones returned to a quiet, normal operational baseline with zero false alarms over a 90-day monitoring window. The Public Address console broadcasts clear voice directives, and the building cleared its statutory Form B compliance inspection without defects.

CASE LOG 02 • PUMP ROOM OVERHAUL







Vertical Wet Riser Welding










## 
High-Rise Pump Station & Wet Riser Manifold Overhaul


Location: Western Suburbs, Mumbai • Building: 22-Storey Commercial & Retail Complex 






Client Profile 
Commercial Block 



System Scope 
150mm Riser + Pumps 



Initial Defect 
Riser Pressure Loss 



Operating Result 
Stable at 7.5 Bar 







### 1. Initial Requirement


A 22-storey commercial complex received a fire compliance notice after pressure in its vertical wet riser dropped below 2 bar. Underground pump check valves had seized open, causing continuous pump cycling and water backflow into raw storage tanks.







### 2. Scope of Work & Execution


Our mechanical team designed, fabricated, and installed a new carbon-steel pump manifold with dual cast-iron non-return valves, resilient-seated gate valves, and pressure relief bypasses. In the riser shaft, 18 corroded coupling gaskets were replaced with high-temperature EPDM grooved seals, and the jockey pump cut-in pressure switch was recalibrated.







### 3. Verified Outcome & Handover


The riser stack was hydro-tested to 10.5 kg/cm² for 2 hours with zero pressure drop. Roof landing valves now maintain a stable 3.5 kg/cm² running flow, fulfilling municipal fire safety standards. Handover documentation included certified Form A clearance and quarterly AMC scheduling.

Title: Building Fire Safety Audit Checklist for Owners and Facility Managers
Last updated: 2026-11-04

A fire safety audit is a structured review of the fire risks and protection arrangements at a particular property. The right checks vary between a housing society, office, school, hospital, warehouse or industrial site. Use this list to prepare for a review, not as a self-issued certificate of compliance.



## 1. Start with the building and its approved plan

Record the use of the building, height, floor count, basements, high-risk rooms, major changes in layout and any change of occupancy. Gather available approved fire plans, fire approvals, system drawings and previous inspection reports. The actual requirement depends on the site and the current rules.



## 2. Check escape routes and exits



- Are corridors, staircases and final exits clear of storage and obstructions? 

- Do exit doors open and operate as intended and are fire doors able to close? 

- Are escape routes and exits clearly marked? 

- Does emergency lighting appear present and in serviceable condition? 

- Are assembly points and access routes for emergency responders kept clear? 

- Are arrangements in place for people who may need help during evacuation? 




## 3. Review active fire protection systems

Check the systems provided for the building: fire pumps, hydrants and risers, landing valves, hose reels, sprinklers, extinguishers, fire alarm panels, detectors, manual call points and any special suppression system. Look for visible damage, missing equipment, leakage, inaccessible cabinets, recurring alarms and records of testing or maintenance.



## 4. Review passive fire protection

Look for fire doors that are wedged open or damaged, missing door closers, unsealed service penetrations, damaged fire barriers and any change that may have compromised a protected shaft or compartment. Repairs or alterations should use products and methods suitable for the specific fire-rated construction and approved design.



## 5. Check housekeeping and common fire risks



- Combustible storage in staircases, electrical rooms and pump rooms. 

- Damaged cables, overloaded sockets or signs of overheating that need qualified electrical attention. 

- Temporary wiring, hot-work activity, gas cylinders or flammable storage relevant to the site. 

- Uncontrolled parking or storage that blocks fire access routes and equipment. 

- Fire doors, ducts and service openings affected by recent renovation work. 




## 6. Check people, training and records

Confirm who is responsible for raising an alarm, guiding occupants, checking assigned areas and meeting emergency responders. Review resident or staff training, fire drill reports, equipment demonstrations, service reports, fault logs and current emergency contact details.



## 7. Convert findings into an action plan

For every defect, record the location, evidence, risk, immediate action, permanent correction, responsible person and target date. Track urgent issues until they are repaired and, where necessary, tested again. If a life-safety system is impaired, use the building’s approved impairment procedure and inform the responsible manager.



## Audit, statutory inspection and certification are not interchangeable

A site review can identify risks and maintenance gaps, but it does not automatically replace statutory approvals or prescribed certificates. In Maharashtra, Form A and Form B have specific roles under the fire-safety framework. Check the official Acts and Rules and the latest Directorate circulars for current requirements.


---

Source: https://samarthfire.in/factory-fire-safety-checklist
Title: Factory & Warehouse Fire Safety Checklist for Owners and Managers
Last updated: 2026-11-04

This checklist is a starting point for owners, facility managers and safety teams. The site’s approved plans, processes, materials and applicable requirements determine the final fire safety arrangements.




## 1. Identify the site’s fire hazards

List the raw materials, finished stock, packaging, fuels, gases, chemicals, process equipment and hot surfaces present. Note where combustible dust, flammable liquids, gas cylinders or heat-producing operations may be involved. Keep the risk review current when the process or storage layout changes.






## 2. Review storage and housekeeping



- Keep aisles, exits, electrical rooms and fire equipment accessible. 

- Store combustible stock away from ignition sources and maintain the clearances required by the approved design. 

- Remove packaging waste and accumulated dust through a planned housekeeping routine. 

- Keep flammable liquids and gases in the approved storage areas with suitable controls. 







## 3. Control hot work and ignition sources

Use a permit and control process for welding, cutting, grinding and other hot work. Identify nearby combustible material, protect openings, provide suitable fire watch arrangements where required and inspect the area after the work is complete. Keep temporary electrical connections and charging areas under control.






## 4. Check installed fire protection systems

Review the systems provided for the particular site: hydrants, risers, sprinklers, pumps, fire alarm panels, detectors, manual call points, suppression systems, extinguishers and passive protection. Confirm that they are accessible and that the maintenance provider records testing, defects and corrective action.






## 5. Match extinguishers to the risks

Different areas may need different extinguisher types. Consider the materials and equipment in the area and follow the approved fire plan, extinguisher label and competent advice. Do not choose a general-purpose extinguisher without checking whether it is suitable for the hazard.






## 6. Check exits, signs and access

Keep emergency exits, stairways, exit doors and fire service access routes clear. Check that fire doors are not held open and that signs and emergency lighting are maintained. Make sure workers and contractors know how to raise the alarm and where to assemble.






## 7. Train workers and contractors

Provide site-specific instruction on raising an alarm, evacuation routes, assembly points, reporting hazards and the safe use of equipment. Fire drills and equipment demonstrations should be planned and supervised by competent people. People should evacuate when a fire is growing or the route is unsafe rather than trying to fight it.






## 8. Keep test and maintenance records

Keep equipment registers, AMC/work orders, inspection and test reports, alarm fault logs, pump records, extinguisher service details, training and drill records, and corrective action logs. Make sure open defects have an owner and target date.






## Important note

A generic checklist cannot confirm statutory compliance for a factory or warehouse. Use the current applicable rules, approved fire plan, relevant standards and directions from the competent authority. The Maharashtra Fire & Emergency Services website publishes the State’s fire-safety legislation and rules.


---

Source: https://samarthfire.in/fire-alarm-amc-checklist
Title: Fire Alarm AMC Checklist: What Should Be Included in Maintenance?
Last updated: 2026-11-04

A fire alarm system includes more than the control panel. Detectors, manual call points, sounders, wiring, power supplies and communication devices all need to work together. A maintenance visit should review the installed system and leave a clear record of what was checked.




## 1. Check the fire alarm control panel

Review the panel’s normal status, displayed faults, disabled or isolated zones/devices, event history, power supply and battery condition. Any fault that remains open should be recorded with its cause if known, the affected area and the planned corrective action.






## 2. Check detectors and manual call points

Inspect the detectors and manual call points fitted in the building. Check for physical damage, paint, dust, obstruction, loose fittings or other conditions that could affect operation. The test method should suit the detector type and manufacturer’s instructions; do not apply smoke or heat casually to a live system.






## 3. Check alarms and notification devices

Confirm the installed sounders, bells, strobes or voice-warning equipment are accessible and can be tested using the building’s approved procedure. Where the system connects to other equipment or a monitoring service, confirm that the interfaces and communication path are covered by the maintenance scope.






## 4. Review wiring, circuits and power supply

Look for visible damage, loose connections, water ingress or changes to the building that may have affected cable routes and devices. Review mains supply and standby batteries. Any electrical work or circuit isolation should be handled by a competent technician under the site’s approved process.






## 5. Keep a fault and repair register

For every fault, note the date, panel message, zone or device, temporary action, technician’s finding, repair and retest result. Do not switch off the system simply to hide a trouble indication. If there are signs of an actual fire, follow the emergency plan immediately.






## 6. Ask for a useful service report

A good report should identify the site and panel, list the devices and circuits checked, record faults and tests, specify work completed and parts replaced, and show any unresolved issue. The next maintenance action should be clear rather than left as a vague “system checked” note.






## How often should fire alarm maintenance take place?

There is no single interval that applies to every panel and every building. The maintenance plan should follow the applicable standard, approved fire strategy, system manufacturer’s instructions, site conditions and directions from the competent authority. The AMC should state what is included and how call-outs and corrective work are handled.






## Questions to ask before signing an AMC



- Which panel, detectors, call points and notification devices are included? 

- How many planned visits and functional tests are covered? 

- Are fault call-outs, replacement parts and after-hours visits included or billed separately? 

- Will the provider maintain a fault register and share a report after each visit? 

- Who is responsible for coordinating any alarm isolation and restoring the system after testing?


---

Source: https://samarthfire.in/fire-alarm-panel-fault-what-to-do
Title: Fire Alarm Panel Fault: What Should a Building Manager Do?
Last updated: 2026-11-04

A fire alarm panel can show an alarm, trouble or supervisory condition. These signals do not mean the same thing. If there is smoke, heat, a burning smell or an activated detector, treat the situation as a possible emergency and follow the building’s evacuation plan. Do not delay an evacuation to investigate the panel.



## What information should the building team record?

From a safe location, note the exact message displayed, zone or device address, time, panel make/model if known, and whether the indication is continuous or intermittent. Inform the designated facility manager, security supervisor or fire-safety coordinator. Do not assume that one fault means every other part of the system is operating normally.



## What should you avoid doing?



- Do not switch off the panel simply to silence a buzzer. 

- Do not repeatedly reset the panel without understanding the reported condition. 

- Do not disconnect a detector, circuit, battery or sounder to make the message disappear. 

- Do not bypass a zone or disable a device unless the approved site procedure and authorised personnel require it. 

- Do not ask an untrained person to open the panel or change wiring. 




## Arrange competent fault rectification

Give the technician the panel message, affected zone or device, time of occurrence, recent power interruptions, renovation work and any previous fault history. Ask the service provider to identify the cause, work performed, parts replaced, remaining impairment and the tests used to verify the repair.



## Confirm the system is restored

After rectification, check that the panel has returned to its normal condition, affected devices and circuits have been tested using the approved method, and temporary impairment measures have been closed by the responsible person. Update the fault register and inform the relevant building stakeholders.



## What if a fire is suspected?

Do not troubleshoot during a suspected fire. Raise the alarm, follow the building’s emergency plan, evacuate where required and call the fire brigade / emergency services. Only attempt firefighting if you are trained, it is safe, the fire is small and you have a clear escape route.



## Reference

Maintenance and testing should follow the installed system’s design, manufacturer instructions, applicable standards and directions of the competent authority. See the Maharashtra Fire & Emergency Services website for official information.

Source: https://samarthfire.in/fire-extinguisher-inspection-checklist-india
Title: Fire Extinguisher Inspection Checklist in India | IS 2190:2024
Last updated: 2026-11-04

An extinguisher should not be treated as a red cylinder that can be forgotten until an emergency. Building teams need a repeatable way to check its location, condition, instructions and service history. The current Indian Standard is IS 2190:2024 , the fifth revision of the code for selection, installation and maintenance of first-aid fire extinguishers.



## How often should extinguishers be checked?

IS 2190:2024 says extinguishers should be checked when first placed in service and thereafter at approximately 90-day intervals . More frequent checks may be needed when the site conditions call for them. This is a periodic check; it is not the same as a full service, refill or hydrostatic pressure test.

The same standard says that, except for the cases listed in its Annex D, extinguishers should receive maintenance once a year and not less than six months apart, at the time of hydrostatic testing, and whenever an inspection indicates that maintenance is required. The correct process depends on the extinguisher category and design.



## The practical inspection checklist



- Location: Is the extinguisher still in its designated position? 

- Access: Is it visible and unobstructed, with its operating instructions facing outwards? 

- Instructions: Can a user read the label and operating directions? 

- Seal and pin: Are the seal and tamper indicators present and undamaged? 

- Fullness: Does the extinguisher appear full, checked by the method suitable for that type? 

- Condition: Is there any visible corrosion, dent, leakage, damage or blocked nozzle? 

- Pressure indicator: Where a gauge or indicator is fitted, is it within the indicated operating range? 

- Mounting: Is the bracket or cabinet secure and undamaged? 

- Records: Are the inspection tag, equipment identification and HPT tag present and legible? 


Record the extinguisher ID, floor or area, check date, condition, defect and action taken. When an extinguisher is discharged, damaged, leaking or outside the operating range, do not leave the location without the protection required by the building’s fire plan. Arrange replacement or appropriate maintenance through a competent service provider.



## Inspection is not the same as HPT

Hydrostatic pressure testing checks whether a cylinder can safely withstand the required test pressure. Its timing and procedure depend on the extinguisher type and the applicable provisions of IS 2190:2024. Avoid using a single “every three years” or “every five years” rule for every cylinder. The service provider should identify the cylinder category, examine its history and follow the relevant standard and manufacturer instructions.



## What should a building’s extinguisher register contain?

A useful register records the equipment number, location, extinguisher type and capacity, access, visible condition, seal and pin status, gauge reading where fitted, hose/nozzle condition, service-tag details, defect and closure date. Keep maintenance reports and HPT records with the register. This makes it easier to identify missed checks and prepare for a building-specific fire-safety review.



## Use the right extinguisher and know when to leave

Different extinguishers are designed for different fuels. Check the cylinder label and the site fire plan; do not assume water, foam, CO₂, dry powder and wet chemical units are interchangeable. Raise the alarm first. Only a trained person should consider using a suitable extinguisher on a small, early-stage fire when the escape route is clear. If the fire grows or conditions are unsafe, evacuate and call emergency services.



## Official reference

Read the BIS IS 2190:2024 standard . This article is a practical overview, not a replacement for the full standard, manufacturer instructions or a competent inspection.


---

Source: https://samarthfire.in/fire-extinguisher-refilling-inspection
Title: Fire Extinguisher Refilling & Inspection: What Building Owners Should Know
Last updated: 2026-11-04

A fire extinguisher is useful only when it is the right type for the risk, easy to reach and in serviceable condition. A quick visual check by the building team is important, but it does not replace maintenance by a competent service provider.




## What should be checked during a routine inspection?

Check that each extinguisher is in its assigned place, visible and not blocked by furniture, storage or parked equipment. The operating instructions should face outwards and be readable. Look for a missing or broken seal, visible damage, corrosion, leakage, a blocked nozzle or a pressure indicator outside its marked operating range (where a gauge is fitted).

Also check the bracket or cabinet, identification number, inspection label and any hydrostatic pressure test (HPT) tag. Record a defect and arrange corrective action; do not quietly return an unserviceable extinguisher to its bracket.






## How often should fire extinguishers be checked?

Indian Standard IS 2190:2024 says extinguishers should be checked when first placed in service and thereafter at approximately 90-day intervals . It also says they should be checked more frequently when circumstances require. These checks are different from a full maintenance visit.

The same standard specifies maintenance once a year, but not less than six months apart, as well as at the time of hydrostatic testing and whenever an inspection indicates it is needed. The exact procedure depends on the extinguisher type and the standard’s relevant category and clauses. Follow the current standard and the manufacturer’s instructions.

Read the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) listing for IS 2190:2024 and the published standard text .






## When does an extinguisher need refilling?

Rechargeable extinguishers should be recharged after any use, even if only a small amount was discharged, or when an inspection or maintenance check identifies a deficiency. Use only the extinguishing medium specified on the extinguisher label and follow the manufacturer’s instructions. A partially used extinguisher should not be put back into service as if it were full.

If a cylinder is leaking, damaged, corroded, discharged or outside its operating range, arrange service and provide suitable replacement protection while it is unavailable.






## What is hydrostatic pressure testing (HPT)?

HPT checks whether an extinguisher cylinder can safely withstand the test pressure specified for its design. The test interval and method are not identical for every extinguisher type. Ask the service provider to check the applicable standard, cylinder markings and previous test record, and to update the tag or service record after testing.






## What should the building keep on record?



- Extinguisher identification number, type, capacity and location 

- Routine inspection date and any defects found 

- Maintenance, refilling and HPT reports 

- Service provider details and work completed 

- Replacement extinguisher details while a unit is away for service 







## What should you ask an extinguisher service provider?

Ask the provider to identify the extinguisher type and condition, explain why it needs refilling or testing, show the relevant service record and return it with its operating instructions and required tags intact. The number and type of extinguishers at a property should be based on the building’s actual risks and applicable requirements—not a one-size-fits-all online estimate.






## Important safety note

Do not dismantle, recharge or pressure-test an extinguisher yourself. If there is a fire, raise the alarm and follow the building’s evacuation plan. Only use a suitable extinguisher on a small fire if you are trained, have a clear escape route and it is safe to do so.


---

Source: https://samarthfire.in/fire-hydrant-and-hose-reel-difference
Title: Fire Hydrant vs Hose Reel: What Is the Difference in a Building?
Last updated: 2026-11-04

A fire hydrant point, a landing valve and a hose reel can all be part of a building’s water-based fire protection arrangements. Their design, location and intended users are not identical. The approved fire plan and system drawings should show which equipment is installed and how it is meant to be used.



## What is a fire hydrant?

A hydrant is an outlet connected to a fire-water supply. External yard hydrants are generally positioned around a site so responders can connect suitable hose equipment. Internal hydrant outlets may be provided through a riser system, with landing valves located at designated floors.



## What is a landing valve?

A landing valve is a valve outlet on a riser, typically installed at a floor landing or designated location. It allows the appropriate hose to be connected to the building’s fire-water supply. Access should be kept clear, identification should be visible and the valve must be maintained as part of the system.



## What is a hose reel?

A hose reel is a permanently arranged length of hose on a drum, generally intended for controlled use on a small fire by a person who has been trained and can operate it safely. It is not a substitute for evacuation, and it is not intended to tackle every fire type or a fire that is spreading.



## How are these items maintained?

Checks should follow the installed system design, applicable Indian Standards and the manufacturer’s instructions. Facility teams should keep the cabinets accessible, look for visible damage and leakage, record defects and arrange competent testing and maintenance. Do not operate valves or discharge water as an informal test.



## Which equipment does your building need?

That depends on occupancy, building height, approved fire plans, water supply and the applicable rules. Do not select equipment based only on a generic online comparison. A site-specific review should identify what is installed and whether it is being maintained correctly.


---

Source: https://samarthfire.in/fire-hydrant-maintenance-checklist-building
Title: Fire Hydrant System Maintenance Checklist for Buildings
Last updated: 2026-11-04

Fire hydrants are not maintained by looking at one red cabinet. A building’s water-based fire protection system may include a tank, main and standby pumps, jockey pump, riser pipes, landing valves, external hydrants, hose reels, hoses, branch pipes and a fire brigade inlet. The maintenance plan should match the system that is actually installed.



## 1. Keep an equipment list and system drawing

Keep a current drawing or asset register showing the pump room, tanks, risers, landing valves, external hydrants, hose reels, isolation valves and fire brigade inlet. Record pump make/model and duty details, valve identification and the normal position of valves that should remain open. This helps the facility team identify missing equipment and report a problem accurately.



## 2. Check visible condition and access



- Keep hydrant points, hose cabinets, pump-room access and fire brigade approach routes clear. 

- Look for leakage, corrosion, impact damage, missing caps, damaged handwheels or damaged pipe supports. 

- Check hose reels, hoses, couplings, branch pipes and nozzles are present and accessible. 

- Ensure landing valves, hydrants and hose cabinets are clearly identified and not blocked by storage or parked vehicles. 

- Report any valve that appears isolated or tampered with; do not change its position without authorisation. 




## 3. Review the pump room and water supply

Check visible controller indications, power availability, water-level records, leakage, unusual noise or vibration and general housekeeping. For diesel pumps, the maintenance plan should cover the fuel, starting battery and other engine checks specified by the manufacturer. Main, standby and jockey pump duties should match the approved design and system documentation.

Functional pump runs and flow tests should be performed by trained personnel using the approved test method. Record the equipment tested, date, readings, observed issues and corrective actions. Do not create a water discharge or operate valves as an informal demonstration.



## 4. Pressure and flow values are design-specific

There is no single pressure or flow figure that can be copied safely to all buildings. The required performance depends on building height, hydraulic calculations, pump duty, the most demanding outlet, the approved design and applicable standards. Use the designated test points and acceptance criteria for that installation, with suitable calibrated instruments.



## 5. Make faults visible and track them to closure

If a pump, tank, riser or outlet is unavailable, record the affected section and inform the responsible building manager. Apply the site’s approved impairment and temporary risk-control procedure, arrange competent repair and retest the system before closing the defect. A repair invoice alone does not prove that the system has been restored and tested.



## 6. Keep these records together



- Current system drawings and equipment register. 

- Pump-run, flow and pressure test reports as applicable to the system. 

- Valve status, inspection and impairment logs. 

- Service reports, parts replaced and calibration records. 

- Defect register with action owner, closure date and retest evidence. 




## Relevant Indian Standards

The Directorate’s July 2026 Form B guidance refers to standards for external and internal hydrants, pumps, hose reels, hoses, couplings and landing valves. Check the latest Maharashtra Fire Services circulars and use the current standards relevant to the system. Testing and isolation must be planned by competent personnel; this checklist is not a substitute for the approved design or maintenance procedure.

Source: https://samarthfire.in/fire-safety-amc-checklist
Title: Fire Safety AMC Checklist: What Should a Maintenance Contract Include?
Last updated: 2026-11-04

An AMC is only useful when the building and the service provider agree what is covered. “Complete fire system maintenance” can mean different things from one contract to another. A good agreement identifies the equipment, schedule, service tasks, response arrangements and reporting in plain language.



## 1. List every system and asset included

Write down the systems, buildings, floors and equipment covered. This may include fire pumps, hydrants, wet risers, landing valves, hose reels, sprinklers, fire alarm panels, detectors, manual call points, extinguishers, gas suppression, fire doors and other passive measures. Identify any item that is excluded or maintained by another provider.



## 2. Agree the maintenance schedule

Different systems have different inspection and test intervals. The contract should state the task and frequency for each group of equipment, based on the applicable Indian Standard, approved fire plan, manufacturer instructions and site conditions. Do not assume that one monthly or quarterly visit automatically covers every legal or technical requirement.



## 3. Define tests and service activities



- What visual inspections and functional checks will be completed? 

- Which pump runs, alarm tests, flow tests or other activities are included? 

- Which tasks need a separate shutdown, permit, water discharge or client approval? 

- Are refilling, HPT, spare parts and consumables included or quoted separately? 

- How will temporary impairments be controlled and reported? 




## 4. Agree fault reporting and response arrangements

The contract should state how the building reports a fault, who receives it, the normal working hours, the response arrangements and what happens when a system is out of service. Avoid vague promises such as “24/7” unless the contract explains what the provider will actually deliver.



## 5. Ask for service reports and a defect register

Each visit should produce a record showing the date, equipment checked, tests carried out, findings, parts used, defects, recommended action and responsible person. Defects should remain open until the building has evidence of correction and any required retest.



## 6. Check how statutory documentation is handled

Clarify whether the AMC includes support for maintenance records and Form B preparation, and which licensed agency is responsible for any prescribed certificate. An AMC by itself does not guarantee that a building complies or that a statutory certificate can be issued. The equipment must be maintained and found in the condition required by the applicable rules and standards.



## Before signing

Compare the scope against the building’s equipment register, approved plans, previous inspection reports and unresolved faults. Ask the provider to identify assumptions and exclusions in writing. This article is a purchasing checklist, not a template contract or a legal opinion.

Source: https://samarthfire.in/fire-safety-audit-vs-fire-noc
Title: Fire Safety Audit vs Fire NOC: What Is the Difference?
Last updated: 2026-11-04

These terms are often mentioned together, but they refer to different things. A building may need an approval at a particular stage, ongoing maintenance of installed systems and separate reviews to identify gaps. The exact requirements depend on the site and applicable law.



## What is a fire safety audit?

A fire safety audit is a review of the building’s risks, fire protection measures, escape routes, housekeeping and supporting records. It can identify equipment that is missing, inaccessible, damaged, overdue for service or not aligned with the approved plan. The scope should be agreed for the specific property.



## What is a Fire NOC or fire approval?

A Fire NOC or fire approval is a separate clearance or approval from the competent authority for the relevant stage and purpose. The documents, drawings and inspections required depend on the building and the type of proposal. A maintenance report does not replace the approval process.



## What are Form A and Form B?



- Form A: associated with the installation of fire-prevention and life-safety measures. 

- Form B: periodic maintenance certificate relating to the systems installed in the building. 


The Directorate issued updated Form B guidelines on 7 July 2026. Check the official circular list and the Acts and Rules page for current instructions.



## Which one does your building need?

Start with the property’s approved fire plan, occupancy, current status and the issue you are trying to resolve. A building owner may need an approval, a periodic maintenance certificate, a site audit, a repair or more than one of these. Ask the competent authority or a currently licensed agency to clarify the requirement for the specific premises.

Source: https://samarthfire.in/fire-safety-training-for-industries
Title: Fire Safety Training for Industrial Workers: A Practical Planning Guide
Last updated: 2026-11-04

Industrial fire safety training should connect the equipment on site with the actions workers are expected to take. A factory, warehouse, utility plant and construction site may have different fuels, machinery, access routes and emergency procedures. Begin with the site risk assessment and approved emergency arrangements.



## 1. Explain how to raise the alarm

Workers should know how to report smoke, heat, a burning smell or another emergency, where manual call points are located where installed, who receives the alarm and how to contact emergency services. Explain what the different alarm indications mean for the site.



## 2. Show the evacuation routes and assembly point

Walk through the designated exits, staircases, final discharge routes and assembly point. Explain the site’s process for headcounts and how supervisors report missing persons. Keep routes and access for emergency responders clear.



## 3. Explain the equipment installed at the site

Identify the types and locations of extinguishers, hydrants, hose reels, sprinklers, fire alarm equipment and any special suppression system. Explain what equipment is intended for which risk and what should be left to trained responders. The operating instructions on the equipment and the site fire plan take priority over a generic demonstration.



## 4. Keep demonstrations controlled

Practical extinguisher demonstrations should be planned, risk-assessed and supervised by competent instructors. Participants need clear instructions, appropriate practice space and a safe escape route. Do not use a live fire or discharge equipment casually as part of an ordinary toolbox talk.



## 5. Include first aid and emergency roles

Discuss how to call for help, who provides first aid within their training and how the site coordinates with emergency responders. CPR or first aid practice should use the correct training equipment and be supervised by an appropriately qualified trainer.



## 6. Record the session and review it

Keep the date, topics, instructor details, attendance and any action items. Review the training after a change in plant layout, work process, staffing or emergency plan. Training supports the fire protection system; it does not replace equipment maintenance or statutory inspections.

Source: https://samarthfire.in/form-b-fire-safety-maharashtra-2026
Title: Form B Fire Safety Certificate Maharashtra: 2026 Guide
Last updated: 2026-11-04

Form B is not a general-purpose Fire NOC. It is a periodic certificate concerning the maintenance of the fire-prevention and life-safety measures in a building. Under the Maharashtra Rules, the licensed agency issues the certificate and the owner or occupier submits it to the Chief Fire Officer or Director, as applicable. Use the latest Directorate guidance, the applicable Rules and the approved fire plan when preparing the submission.



## What changed in the 2026 guidance?

The Directorate of Maharashtra Fire & Emergency Services lists a circular titled Guidelines to issue Form B , dated 7 July 2026 . The circular explains the six-month reporting periods and supporting evidence expected from the owner/occupier and licensed agency. It also explains that the maintenance schedule for individual equipment continues to apply during the Form B cycle; the certificate period does not replace the service intervals required by relevant standards.



## Which period does each Form B cover?

Submission cycle | Maintenance period described in the 2026 guidance |
January | 1 July to 31 December of the preceding year |
July | 1 January to 30 June of the current year |


Confirm the current submission route and any subsequent circular with the local Chief Fire Officer or nominated officer. Do not rely on an old form template or another building’s filing date as a substitute for current instructions.



## How long does Form B remain valid?

The Directorate says Form B remains valid until the next scheduled maintenance of equipment under the relevant Indian Standard and/or until the next Form B is issued by the same licensed agency or another agency appointed by the owner/occupier, subject to the earlier maintenance contract remaining in force. This means the next maintenance due date for individual equipment still matters; Form B is not a blanket six-month deferral of every service task.



## What should you prepare before the inspection?

The Directorate describes the following as a minimum set of supporting records (the list is not exhaustive):



- A covering letter on the owner/occupier’s letterhead. 

- The prescribed Form B and relevant appendices for the installed fire-fighting, detection/alarm and passive systems. 

- A copy of the AMC/CAMC order without the amount, or a work-order confirmation stating the maintenance period, systems covered and name of the appointed agency. 

- Service/checking/test reports for the relevant month, quarter or half-year, as applicable, signed by the licensed agency representative and owner/occupier on the day of testing. 

- The latest site inspection report, digitally signed by the representatives of both parties. 

- A copy of the licensed agency’s current Directorate licence. The digital signature on Form B should match the signature on the licence issued by the Director. 

- Other records called for by the applicable appendices and current directions. The circular includes examples of dated photographic evidence for system checks and mock-drill records where applicable. 


The exact documents depend on the systems installed and the appendices that apply to the building. The circular also states that Form B should not have words added or removed, and that the Maharashtra Fire Service logo should not be used on the certificate. A report should describe work actually carried out; do not create test records or sign off an inspection that did not take place.



## One licensed agency for each system group

The 7 July 2026 guidelines state that, throughout one building or occupancy, water-based fire-fighting systems such as pumps, hydrants and sprinklers shall be maintained by one single agency . Detection, alarm and suppression systems are likewise to be maintained by one agency for the entire building/occupancy. Passive measures—including fire doors, sealant, pressurisation and smoke management—are also to be maintained by one agency for the entire building/occupancy. The Directorate explains that splitting responsibility among agencies can make it harder to maintain the integrity of the complete system.



## What should the maintenance inspection look at?

The equipment depends on the building. A site may have hydrants and wet risers, fire pumps, sprinklers, fire alarm and detection systems, extinguishers, smoke management, fire doors, seals or other passive measures. Each item needs the inspection or test appropriate to its standard, design and manufacturer instructions.

The Directorate’s July 2026 guidance refers to current Indian Standards for these systems, including standards for extinguishers, hydrants, pumps, hose reels, hoses, landing valves, sprinklers and fire alarm systems. A single generic checklist or one pressure value cannot cover every building.



## Form B is not a one-day paperwork exercise

Maintenance has to happen throughout the year. Some equipment may have daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, half-yearly or yearly tasks depending on the applicable standard and site plan. The Form B cycle does not cancel the next maintenance date. Keep a defect register and close faults with evidence of repair and retesting.



## Form A, Form B and Fire NOC are different



- Form A: associated with installation of fire-prevention and life-safety measures. 

- Form B: periodic maintenance certificate for the measures installed. 

- Fire NOC / approval: a separate approval or clearance issued for the relevant stage and purpose. 


Use the exact prescribed form and current digital-signature process. A quotation, AMC or service report is not itself a Form B certificate.



## Official references

Read the Directorate’s 7 July 2026 Guidelines to issue Form B (PDF) , the official circular index and the official Fire Acts and Rules page . This article is general information; requirements depend on the building and current directions of the competent authority.

Source: https://samarthfire.in/housing-society-fire-drill-planning-guide
Title: Housing Society Fire Drill: How to Plan a Safe Evacuation
Last updated: 2026-11-04

A well-run fire drill helps residents and security staff understand what to do before an emergency happens. A drill should follow the building’s approved emergency plan and be managed so that it does not create unnecessary risk or block access for emergency responders.



## 1. Review the building’s evacuation plan

Identify the approved exit routes, staircases, final exits, refuge areas where provided, assembly point and fire brigade access. Check that the route is accessible and is not blocked by parked vehicles, stored items or temporary work. Do not invent a route that conflicts with the building’s approved plan.



## 2. Assign roles before the drill



- Nominate a drill coordinator and floor or wing wardens. 

- Assign people to raise the alarm, guide occupants and report floor status. 

- Decide how the assembly point will record attendance and report anyone unaccounted for. 

- Discuss assistance arrangements with residents who may need support, respecting their needs and consent. 




## 3. Inform residents and staff

Tell residents the date and time window, what the alarm signal means, which routes to use and where the assembly point is located. Include security guards, housekeeping teams, domestic workers, visitors and contractors. Make instructions available in a format people can understand.



## 4. Conduct the exercise safely

Use the site’s approved alarm and drill procedure, and make sure the coordinator can stop the exercise if a real emergency occurs. People should move calmly and use the designated stairs. Do not use lifts unless the building’s approved plan specifically provides a designated evacuation lift and trained procedure. Keep exits and fire brigade access routes clear.

Do not use live flames or smoke-producing materials for an ordinary resident drill. Do not discharge extinguishers or operate hydrants for a demonstration unless the activity has been risk-assessed and is supervised by competent trainers.



## 5. Take a headcount and record observations

At the assembly point, wardens should report whether their assigned areas have cleared and whether anyone is unaccounted for. Record bottlenecks, unclear signage, alarm audibility issues, blocked doors, confusion about routes and any assistance that was needed.



## 6. Close improvement actions

Prepare a short report with the observations, action owner and target date. Share the key learning with residents and repeat or update the exercise when the building or its emergency plan changes. The Directorate’s July 2026 Form B guidance also refers to periodic mock fire safety drills and supporting attendance records.



## Remember

A drill is not a replacement for maintenance of alarms, hydrants, sprinklers, extinguishers or fire doors. Keep equipment service records current and address defects through the building’s approved process.
